The \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/usage-cost-api\",\"children\":\"Usage and Cost API\"}],\" breaks spend down by model and by cached versus uncached tokens.\"]}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"strong\",null,{\"children\":\"Try the effort ladder.\"}],\" Run one hard task at medium and then at high. Run one mechanical task at low.\"]}],\"\\n\"]}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"h3\",null,{\"id\":\"reading-a-session\",\"children\":\"Reading a session\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Check three things in /usage at the end of a task.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"ul\",null,{\"children\":[\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"strong\",null,{\"children\":\"Cache share.\"}],\" For a long session it should be high. If it's low, look for a long pause, a model switch, an MCP server connected partway through or, on a cloud provider or gateway, a change of effort. The prompt cache line often names the likely cause of the last miss.\"]}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"strong\",null,{\"children\":\"Output against input.\"}],\" A lot of output on a small change usually means the effort level is too high for the task, or the model is retrying.\"]}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"strong\",null,{\"children\":\"Total input against the size of the conversation.\"}],\" If the total is many times the size of the conversation, the session took many turns, and the conversation is worth reading to find where the loop repeated.\"]}],\"\\n\"]}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"For a baseline, the Claude Code costs docs give an average across enterprise deployments of about $13 per developer per active day, and under $30 per active day for 90% of users. A session that costs well above your own normal level is worth reviewing.\"}],\"\\n\"]}]\n3a:[\"$\",\"section\",null,{\"className\":\"art-section\",\"data-reveal\":\"\",\"style\":\"$2b:0:props:style\",\"id\":\"what-a-task-costs-on-opus-5-5-s6\",\"children\":[[\"$\",\"h2\",null,{\"id\":\"keep-in-mind\",\"children\":[\"KEEP IN MIND\"]}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"ul\",null,{\"children\":[\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"Use medium effort for well-scoped daily work.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"Give the model a way to check its work, and start changes that span files in plan mode.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"When medium stalls, raise effort to high. With an API key or a subscription the change keeps your cache. On a cloud provider or gateway, change it at a break.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"If xhigh hits the same problem twice, switch to Fable 5.1. Switch back once it's solved.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"Put search and log-reading subagents on Sonnet or Haiku. Keep code edits on Opus 5.5.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"Keep a long session moving, so its cache stays warm.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"Use /clear between unrelated tasks, and /compact at a break with a note on what to keep.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"strong\",null,{\"children\":\"The one that matters most:\"}],\" run one real task on each model and compare what /usage reports. Your own numbers are the ones to trust.\"]}],\"\\n\"]}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"I hope this post was helpful. If your limits don’t go further on Opus 5.5 than on Opus 5, tell us with /feedback.\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":[\"Further reading: \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs\",\"children\":\"Manage costs effectively\"}],\" · \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config\",\"children\":\"Model configuration\"}],\" · \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://claude.com/blog/claude-model-and-effort-level-in-claude-code\",\"children\":\"Choosing a Claude model and effort level in Claude Code\"}],\" · \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort\",\"children\":\"Effort\"}],\" · \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching\",\"children\":\"Prompt caching\"}],\" · \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://claude.com/blog/maximizing-the-value-of-your-claude-code-sessions\",\"children\":\"Maximizing the value of your Claude Code sessions\"}]]}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":[\"$\",\"em\",null,{\"children\":\"With thanks to Michael Segner, Kacie Jenkins and Molly Vorwerck for their reviews.\"}]}]]}]\n79:\"CostCalculatorFigure\"\n7a:I[12324,[\"$2\",\"$3\",\"$20\",\"$21\"],\"$79\"]\n3b:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"strong\",null,{\"children\":\"Long runs end with a report.\"}],\" Opus 5.5 closes a long run with what it changed, what it found, and what it needs from you. That can save money too, because you rerun a session less often when you can see what happened.\"]}]\n3e:[\"$\",\"$L7a\",null,{\"data\":\"$37:props:children:4:props:data\",\"label\":\"FIG C\",\"caption\":\"$undefined\"}]\n41:[\"$\",\"h4\",null,{\"id\":\"when-medium-fixes-one-layer\",\"children\":\"When medium fixes one layer\"}]\n42:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"The clearest sign you need more effort is a fix that stops at one layer.\"}]\n43:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Say a field is renamed in an API handler. At medium, the model updates the handler, the handler's tests pass, and the client still sends the old field. It did what it was asked. It just didn't read far enough to find the second caller. At high, it spends more turns reading call sites before it writes, and it changes both layers in one pass.\"}]\n44:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"A check can catch the same bug. If the model can run a test that goes through the client, the old field fails that test on the turn it was written, at medium. So before you raise effort, check whether the model has a way to check its work. A test run costs one turn and its output. More effort adds thinking to every turn.\"}]\n45:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"If upgrading effort levels and adding checks doesn’t work, then switch to a bigger model.\"}]\n46:[\"$\",\"h4\",null,{\"id\":\"changing-effort-mid-session\",\"children\":\"Changing effort mid-session\"}]\n47:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"In Claude Code, run /effort with a level, for example /effort high. /effort status prints the current level. You can change it mid-task, and the new level applies to the next request.\"}]\n48:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"On Opus 5.5 with an API key or a Claude subscription, changing effort keeps the cache. You can raise it for one hard step and lower it again without rewriting the conversation. On Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform or a Claude apps gateway, a change of effort still clears the cached conversation, and the next request pays the cache-write price on all of it. Thinking is always on for Opus 5.5, so there's no thinking setting to change.\"}]\n49:[\"$\",\"h3\",null,{\"id\":\"choose-the-right-model-for-your-work\",\"children\":\"Choose the right model for your work\"}]\n4a:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Model choice sets the price of every token in a session, so it moves the bill more than effort does. It also reaches further. Every subagent that inherits the main model inherits its price too. Most days need three models: a small one for lookups, Opus 5.5 for work you supervise closely, and a bigger one for the hardest tasks.\"}]\n4b:[\"$\",\"figure\",null,{\"className\":\"art-fig\",\"children\":[[\"$\",\"img\",null,{\"className\":\"fg\",\"src\":\"/media/f08757b9a91bce794fda0b6e3cd0deacede7783ce9db0097a67a47606e6900a4.png\",\"alt\":\"Three models in order of cost, with bars that show order of cost only: Haiku or Sonnet for lookups and subagents, Opus 5.5 as the daily driver, and Fable 5.1 for the hardest work, each with the kinds of work it suits.\",\"loading\":\"lazy\",\"decoding\":\"async\",\"width\":2160,\"height\":1692,\"style\":{\"display\":\"block\",\"width\":\"100%\",\"aspectRatio\":\"2160 / 1692\"}}],null]}]\n4c:[\"$\",\"h4\",null,{\"id\":\"opus-55-as-the-daily-driver\",\"children\":\"Opus 5.5 as the daily driver\"}]\n4d:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Use Opus 5.5 for work you supervise: feature work across a few files, debugging, and code review with follow-up edits. You read what it does and step in when it drifts, so the loop stays short.\"}]\n4e:[\"$\",\"h4\",null,{\"id\":\"moving-up-to-fable-51\",\"children\":\"Moving up to Fable 5.1\"}]\n4f:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"strong\",null,{\"children\":\"Move up to Fable 5.1 when the result matters more than the token price.\"}],\" For example long runs you won't supervise, problems with no existing pattern in the codebase, and large changes that coordinate many subagents. Don't wait for a third failure. If Opus 5.5 on xhigh hits the same problem twice, switch, and switch back once it's solved. For interactive work, Opus 5.5 is a better fit as it has lower latency and costs less.\"]}]\n50:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Fable 5.1 lists at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output, two and a half times the Opus 5.5 price. Its cache reads cost $0.25 per million, only 1.25 times the Opus 5.5 rate, because they bill at 0.025 times its input price. So the gap is smallest on a long, cache-heavy run, and largest on a task that writes a lot.\"}]\n51:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":[\"Switch at a natural break. The cache belongs to the previous model, so expect the first turn on the new model to pay the write price on the whole conversation. Run /compact first, or start a fresh session with a short written plan, to make that turn smaller. Run \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config\",\"children\":\"/model\"}],\" with an alias or a model name to switch. /model also saves your choice as the default for new sessions, so switch back when the hard part is done.\"]}]\n52:[\"$\",\"h4\",null,{\"id\":\"moving-down-for-lookups\",\"children\":\"Moving down for lookups\"}]\n53:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"strong\",null,{\"children\":\"Move down to Sonnet or Haiku for lookups, not for writing code:\"}],\" subagents that search and summarize, reading logs and test output, and \\\"where is this defined\\\" questions. For a mechanical edit across many files, keep Opus 5.5 and set effort to low. The edit stays on the model that writes the rest of your code, at a lower cost per turn.\"]}]\n54:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":[\"To put a \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents\",\"children\":\"subagent\"}],\" on a smaller model, set model: haiku or model: sonnet in its definition. To put every subagent on one model, set the CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL environment variable. A model named in a subagent's definition overrides the variable. A subagent with no model setting runs on your main model, unless the variable is set.\"]}]\n55:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Each subagent runs in its own context window and hands back a summary, so its file reads stay out of your main conversation. It still pays for its own tokens, so the model setting decides what that spend costs.\"}]\n56:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":[\"Agent teams, an experimental feature, multiply this. Each teammate is a separate Claude Code instance with its own context window, and it keeps using tokens until it exits. Our \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs\",\"children\":\"costs docs\"}],\" put a team at about seven times the tokens of a standard session when teammates run in plan mode. Keep teams small, keep each task self-contained, and shut teammates down when their part is done.\"]}]\n57:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"The tradeoff: a small model that misreads a search result sends the main model after the wrong file, and the main model pays for the detour. Keep the small model on work where a mistake is cheap to spot, like finding files, running tests and reading logs.\"}]\n58:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Keep judgment calls on the main model. The opusplan alias splits the work a different way: Opus plans in plan mode, and Sonnet carries out the plan. That puts the code edits on Sonnet, the opposite of the advice above. Measure it on your own tasks before you make it a default.\"}]\n59:[\"$\",\"h3\",null,{\"id\":\"check-your-prompts-when-you-migrate\",\"children\":\"Check your prompts when you migrate\"}]\n5a:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":[\"Instructions written for an older model can make Opus 5.5 write more and repeat tool calls. Run /claude-api prompt-audit in Claude Code to check your Claude Code setup, such as your skills and CLAUDE.md file, for these \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://claude.com/blog/reducing-cost-and-improving-performance-with-claude-platform\",\"children\":\"prompting anti-patterns\"}],\". It also checks the code of an app you build on the Claude Platform.\"]}]\n5b:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"We tested this on a migration from Opus 4.8 to Opus 5.5, using an internal customer support benchmark of 44 tickets whose prompt had several of these patterns. The move to Opus 5.5, at low effort, cut the benchmark's cost by about 18%. Running prompt-audit cut it by a further 9%, to about 25% below the Opus 4.8 starting point. The audit removed ritual instructions that made the model write more and repeat tool calls: a mandatory six-step procedure, a scratchpad rule, a verify-twice rule, and instructions that contradicted each other.\"}]\n5c:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"That result comes from one benchmark, so treat it as an example rather than a number to expect. Run the audit, then compare /usage on a real task before and after (see Measure it yourself).\"}]\n5d:[\"$\",\"h3\",null,{\"id\":\"caching-and-compaction\",\"children\":\"Caching and compaction\"}]\n5e:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Claude Code handles caching and compaction for you. How you run a session decides how much they save.\"}]\n5f:[\"$\",\"h4\",null,{\"id\":\"how-the-cache-works\",\"children\":\"How the cache works\"}]\n60:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Claude Code caches the parts of a request that repeat, such as the system prompt, tool definitions, and the conversation so far.\"}]\n61:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"On Opus 5.5 a cached read costs 5% of a fresh input token. Writing to the cache costs more than a fresh read, at 1.25 times the input price for a five-minute cache and twice the input price for a one-hour cache, on today's pricing. Each hit resets the lifetime at no charge.\"}]\n62:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"In Claude Code the lifetime depends on how you pay. On a Claude subscription it's an hour. On an API key or a cloud provider it's five minutes by default, and a subscription drops to five minutes once it's drawing on usage credits.\"}]\n63:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"At 120K tokens of context, a five-minute write on Opus 5.5 costs about $0.60 and a read about $0.02. One write costs as much as 25 reads. On an API key, a six-minute coffee break turns the next $0.02 read into a $0.60 write. A one-hour write at the same size costs about $0.96, and on the API you can pay that premium to cover the gaps in your day.\"}]\n64:[\"$\",\"h4\",null,{\"id\":\"session-shape-and-hit-rate\",\"children\":\"Session shape and hit rate\"}]\n65:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"The cache stores a prefix, so it can reuse only the part of a request that matches the previous one from the start.\"}]\n66:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"A steady session appends to the end of the conversation on every turn and keeps its hit rate high. Anything that changes an earlier part of the request lowers it. Changing the tool definitions clears the whole cache, and a change to the system prompt clears it from that point on, which is almost everything.\"}]\n67:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"In practice, expect a cache write when:\"}]\n68:[\"$\",\"ul\",null,{\"children\":[\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"You pause longer than the cache lifetime;\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"You change effort on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform or a gateway, where the level is part of what the cache matches;\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"You turn on fast mode for the first time in a conversation, which changes part of what the cache matches;\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"You connect or disconnect an MCP server, which can change what loads at the start of each request;\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"You switch models, since the new model starts from an empty cache; and\"}],\"\\n\",[\"$\",\"li\",null,{\"children\":\"The conversation is compacted, which rewrites the history the cache matched.\"}],\"\\n\"]}]\n69:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"So set these up when the session starts, and leave them alone while it works.\"}]\n6a:[\"$\",\"h4\",null,{\"id\":\"why-long-sessions-cost-more-per-turn\",\"children\":\"Why long sessions cost more per turn\"}]\n6b:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Every turn resends the whole context, so a turn costs more as the context grows, even with a warm cache. At 20K tokens of context a turn's cache read costs about $0.004 on Opus 5.5. At 150K it costs about $0.03, and 30 turns at that size spend $0.90 on reads alone. The same 30 turns at 20K cost about $0.12. On Claude 4.6 and later models a bigger context window doesn't change the price per token, so the cost comes entirely from resending the conversation.\"}]\n6c:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Much of that context is left over from earlier work: a stack trace from an hour ago, a file you've finished with, the output of a test run you've since fixed. It's all still sent on every turn.\"}]\n6d:[\"$\",\"h4\",null,{\"id\":\"compaction-compact-and-clear\",\"children\":\"Compaction, /compact and /clear\"}]\n6e:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"When a session gets close to its context limit, Claude Code summarizes older history so later turns send less. Run /autocompact with a token count to change how full the context gets before that happens.\"}]\n6f:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Two commands let you do this yourself. /clear empties the conversation and costs nothing, so use it when you move to unrelated work. /compact keeps continuity and costs one request. It reads the conversation it summarizes, and you can say what to keep, for example /compact keep the failing test names and the schema change.\"}]\n70:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"A rough price for compacting at 150K tokens is about $0.25. That's the read, a summary of a few thousand output tokens, and a new cache write on the shorter context. Each later turn saves about $0.025 in reads, so the compaction pays for itself within about ten turns. A compaction just before you finish costs more than it saves.\"}]\n71:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"That price assumes a warm cache. While the cache is warm, the summary request reads the conversation from it, so compact before a break, not after one. After a break longer than the cache lifetime, the same /compact reads the whole conversation again and writes it back to the cache. At 150K tokens on a five-minute cache, the input alone comes to about $0.75. If you've gone down a path you want to drop, /rewind to an earlier turn instead. While the cache is warm, that returns to a prefix that's already cached.\"}]\n72:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"The summary also loses detail. A compaction in the middle of a debugging session can drop the one log line that mattered. Compact at a natural break, and when the next step depends on something specific, say so in the /compact instruction.\"}]\n73:[\"$\",\"h4\",null,{\"id\":\"what-loads-before-you-type\",\"children\":\"What loads before you type\"}]\n74:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":[\"Your \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory\",\"children\":\"CLAUDE.md file\"}],\" loads into the context at the start of every session, so each line in it is part of what every turn resends. The \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs\",\"children\":\"costs docs\"}],\" suggest keeping it under 200 lines. MCP tool definitions are deferred. Only tool names and server instructions load at the start, and a full definition loads when its tool is used. Run /mcp to see which servers are connected, and turn off the ones you aren't using.\"]}]\n75:[\"$\",\"h4\",null,{\"id\":\"the-rest-of-the-bill\",\"children\":\"The rest of the bill\"}]\n76:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"The table lists the other billing rules that affect a Claude Code session, with a link to the docs where one exists.\"}]\n77:[\"$\",\"p\",null,{\"children\":\"Fast mode runs Opus 5.5 up to 2.5 times faster, at twice the standard price: $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output. On a Claude subscription it's billed to usage credits, not your plan limits. The first request after you turn it on pays the fast-mode input price on the whole conversation, uncached. So turn it on at the start of a session, not deep into one.\"}]\n78:[\"$\",\"div\",null,{\"className\":\"art-table\",\"children\":[\"$\",\"table\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"thead\",null,{\"children\":[\"$\",\"tr\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"th\",null,{\"scope\":\"col\",\"children\":\"What the bill counts\"}],[\"$\",\"th\",null,{\"scope\":\"col\",\"children\":\"How it works\"}]]}]}],[\"$\",\"tbody\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"tr\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"td\",null,{\"children\":\"Cache lifetime\"}],[\"$\",\"td\",null,{\"children\":[\"In Claude Code, one hour on a subscription; five minutes on an API key or cloud provider, or once a subscription draws on usage credits. Each hit resets the lifetime. The API offers a one-hour cache at a higher write price. \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs\",\"children\":\"Costs docs (Claude Code lifetime) and prompt caching docs\"}]]}]]}],[\"$\",\"tr\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"td\",null,{\"children\":\"Cache writes\"}],[\"$\",\"td\",null,{\"children\":[\"1.25× the input price for a five-minute cache and 2× for a one-hour cache, on today's API pricing. \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing\",\"children\":\"Pricing docs\"}]]}]]}],[\"$\",\"tr\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"td\",null,{\"children\":\"Thinking\"}],[\"$\",\"td\",null,{\"children\":[\"Billed as output tokens, including thinking that isn't returned to you. \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking\",\"children\":\"Extended thinking docs\"}]]}]]}],[\"$\",\"tr\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"td\",null,{\"children\":\"Effort\"}],[\"$\",\"td\",null,{\"children\":[\"Applies to every output token: text, tool calls and thinking. \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort\",\"children\":\"Effort docs\"}]]}]]}],[\"$\",\"tr\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"td\",null,{\"children\":\"Auto-compaction\"}],[\"$\",\"td\",null,{\"children\":[\"Runs as the context window nears its limit. /autocompact with a token count sets the threshold. \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window\",\"children\":\"Context window docs\"}]]}]]}],[\"$\",\"tr\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"td\",null,{\"children\":\"Subagents and agent teams\"}],[\"$\",\"td\",null,{\"children\":[\"A subagent works in its own context window and returns a summary. Agent teams in plan mode use about 7× the tokens of a standard session. \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs\",\"children\":\"Context window and costs docs\"}]]}]]}],[\"$\",\"tr\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"td\",null,{\"children\":\"Batch API\"}],[\"$\",\"td\",null,{\"children\":[\"Half price on input and output tokens for requests sent through the Message Batches API. \",[\"$\",\"a\",null,{\"href\":\"https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing\",\"children\":\"Batch processing docs\"}]]}]]}],[\"$\",\"tr\",null,{\"children\":[[\"$\",\"td\",null,{\"children\":\"Typical spend today\"}],[\"$\",\"td\",null,{\"children\":[\"Average: about $13 per developer per active day across enterprise deployments. For 90% of users, cost stays below $30 per active day.
